title: Will vs Going To

vocab.ex: I think it will rain tomorrow.
I'll answer the phone — that's a spontaneous decision.
I will help you, I promise.
I'm going to visit my parents this weekend.
It's just an intention, not a fixed plan.
Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.
Going to shows something decided before speaking.
Will shows something decided right now.
I'll carry your bags for you.
I think it will be a great trip.
It will probably rain later.
I'm definitely going to finish this today.
Look at those dark clouds!
That's a clear sign it's going to rain.
I'm going to visit my grandmother next week.
The phone is ringing — I'll get it!
The weather forecast says it will be sunny.
I promise I will call you tonight.
Don't worry, I will help you with this.
In my opinion, the team will win.
This is a general prediction about the future.
I've already decided — I'm going to quit my job.
There's clear evidence it's going to happen.
He spontaneously decided to help.
I've decided right now — I'll do it.
She planned it beforehand.
I expect it will be busy tomorrow.
What are your weekend plans?
It will surely rain later today.
She is about to leave — she's going to miss the bus!

grammar.title: Will vs Going To: Escolhendo a Forma Certa
rules: WILL para previsão geral (opinião): I think it will rain tomorrow.
WILL para decisão espontânea (decidida na hora de falar): The phone is ringing — I'll answer it!
WILL para promessas: Don't worry, I will help you.
GOING TO para planos/intenções (decididos ANTES de falar): I'm going to visit my parents.
GOING TO para previsão com evidência visível: Look at those clouds — it's going to rain!

rows: I'm going to visit my parents.

quiz.q: The phone is ringing — I ___ (will) answer it!
Look at those clouds — it ___ (going to) rain!
I've already decided — I'm ___ (going to) change jobs.
